uble vitamins: A, K, E, and D
For the DRIs for vitamins A, K, (IOM, 2001) and for vitamin E (IOM, 2000) (Table 6), the AI for infants aged 0–6 months was based
on the human milk model as previously described. For vitamins A, K, and E, the AI for infants aged 7–12 months was extrapolated
up from the values for infants aged 0–6 months using a reference weight for infants at this age. Notably, the AI was set assuming that
the infants had received a prophylactic injection of vitamin K just after birth, a routine in North America since vitamin K is not
readily transferred to the fetus while in utero, and human milk is relatively low in vitamin K.
